name: Matar Paneer

ingredients.name: Green peas (matar), fresh shelled or frozen
Tomato (tamatar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 medium ripe tomato, finely chopped or grated

ingredients.name: Warm water, for soaking the paneer

equipment: Grater (for ginger, garlic and, if you prefer a smoother gravy, the tomato)
Small bowl, for soaking the paneer cubes
Kadai or medium heavy pan with a lid (about 20 cm)
Measuring spoons and a measuring cup (a normal teaspoon and a steel glass are fine stand-ins)

steps.title: Cube the paneer
steps.text: Cut 75 g paneer into 2 cm cubes.
steps.visualCue: 10–12 even cubes, about the size of a dice
steps.cameraCheck: The paneer cubes on the board
steps.videoShot: A knife slicing a paneer block into cubes.

steps.title: Soak the paneer
steps.text: Put the cubes in a bowl and cover them with about 1 cup warm (not boiling) water. Leave them while you cook.
steps.tip: Soaking keeps packet paneer soft so it does not turn rubbery in the gravy.
steps.visualCue: Cubes fully under water
steps.videoShot: Warm water poured over paneer cubes.

steps.title: Thaw or rinse the peas
steps.text: Measure 60 g peas (a little under ½ cup). If frozen, rinse them under running water in a sieve; if fresh, rinse and drain.
steps.visualCue: Bright green peas, no ice crystals
steps.videoShot: Water running over green peas in a sieve.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Finely chop ½ medium onion (60 g).
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces, about ½ cup
steps.videoShot: A knife chopping onion fine.

steps.title: Grate the ginger and garlic
steps.text: Grate ½-inch ginger (4 g) and 2 small garlic cloves (4 g).
steps.visualCue: A small heap of pale, wet paste
steps.videoShot: Ginger rubbed on the grater.

steps.title: Prepare the green chilli
steps.text: Slit 1 small green chilli lengthwise (or chop it fine for more heat).
steps.visualCue: Chilli split open, seeds showing
steps.videoShot: A knife slitting a green chilli.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Finely chop or grate 1 medium ripe tomato (100 g), discarding the skin if grating.
steps.tip: Use a fully red tomato; an unripe one makes the gravy sour.
steps.visualCue: Pulpy red tomato, about ½ cup
steps.videoShot: Tomato rubbed on a grater, skin left in the hand.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat and add 2 tsp (10 g) oil.
steps.visualCue: Oil shimmers and flows easily when the pan is tilted
steps.videoShot: Oil swirling in a heating kadai.

steps.title: Temper the cumin and bay leaf
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp cumin seeds and 1 bay leaf.
steps.tip: If the cumin turns black at once, the oil is too hot; lower the heat.
steps.visualCue: Cumin sizzles and turns one shade darker; nutty smell
steps.videoShot: Cumin crackling in hot oil.

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and stir on medium heat.
steps.tip: Stir every 30 seconds; golden onion gives the home-style gravy its sweetness and colour.
steps.visualCue: Soft and light golden-brown at the edges, sweet smell
steps.videoShot: Spatula turning golden onion.

steps.title: Add ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and the green chilli.
steps.visualCue: The raw garlic smell goes
steps.cameraCheck: The paste mixed into the onion
steps.videoShot: The paste stirred into the onion.

steps.title: Add the powders
steps.text: Lower the heat and add a big pinch of turmeric, ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and ¾ tsp coriander powder. Stir.
steps.tip: Powders burn in seconds; if the pan looks dry, add 1 tbsp water before the tomato.
steps.visualCue: The onion turns orange-red; spices smell toasted, not burnt
steps.videoShot: Powders sprinkled over the onion and stirred.

steps.title: Add the tomato and salt
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and 2 g (⅓ tsp) salt. Turn the heat back to medium and stir.
steps.visualCue: Red tomato spread through the masala
steps.videoShot: Tomato tipped into the kadai.

steps.title: Cook the masala soft
steps.text: Cover and cook on medium-low, stirring and mashing every minute.
steps.visualCue: Tomato completely mushy, no raw pieces
steps.cameraCheck: The mashed masala with the lid lifted
steps.videoShot: The spatula mashing soft tomato.

steps.title: Cook until the oil separates
steps.text: Uncover and keep stirring on medium-low.
steps.tip: This is the step that decides the taste; a gravy that has not reached this stage tastes raw and sour.
steps.visualCue: The masala turns thick and glossy and small drops of oil appear at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The edge of the masala showing oil
steps.videoShot: Close-up of oil beading at the edge of the masala.

steps.title: Add the peas
steps.text: Add the 60 g peas and stir them into the masala.
steps.visualCue: Green peas coated in red masala
steps.videoShot: Peas tipped in and stirred.

steps.title: Add the water
steps.text: Pour in 150 ml water and stir, scraping the bottom.
steps.visualCue: A thin, orange gravy
steps.videoShot: Water poured into the kadai.

steps.title: Simmer the peas
steps.text: Bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low.
steps.visualCue: A pea squashes easily between two fingers; gravy slightly thickened
steps.cameraCheck: One pea pressed between your fingers
steps.videoShot: A pea being squashed on a spoon.

steps.title: Drain the paneer
steps.text: Drain the soaked paneer cubes.
steps.visualCue: Soft, white, slightly puffed cubes
steps.videoShot: Water tipped out of the paneer bowl.

steps.title: Add the paneer
steps.text: Add the cubes to the gravy and stir gently.
steps.tip: Stir with a gentle fold, not a scrape, so the cubes do not break.
steps.visualCue: Cubes coated in gravy, still whole
steps.videoShot: Paneer cubes slid into the kadai.

steps.title: Simmer with the paneer
steps.text: Simmer uncovered on low.
steps.visualCue: Gravy coats the back of a spoon; paneer heated through (do not boil longer, or it firms up)
steps.videoShot: A spoon lifted out of the gravy, coated.

steps.title: Taste and adjust
steps.text: Taste and add a pinch more salt only if needed; add 2–3 tbsp hot water if the gravy is too thick.
steps.visualCue: Gently spiced, slightly tangy, sweet from the peas
steps.videoShot: A spoon of gravy lifted for tasting.

steps.title: Finish with garam masala and kasuri methi
steps.text: Sprinkle ¼ tsp garam masala and crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the kadai. Stir and turn off the heat.
steps.visualCue: Green flecks and a warm, sweet smell
steps.cameraCheck: The kasuri methi on the gravy
steps.videoShot: Palms rubbing kasuri methi over the pan.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Remove the bay leaf, transfer to a bowl and scatter 2 tsp chopped coriander leaves on top.
steps.tip: The gravy thickens as it rests for 5 minutes; that is normal.
steps.visualCue: Orange-red gravy with white paneer, green peas and green garnish
steps.videoShot: Coriander scattered over the bowl, steam rising.

reasons: about 19 g protein and about 7 g fibre for 400 kcal, no added sugar, no deep-frying, real vegetables (peas, tomato, onion) and only 2 tsp oil. Points off for saturated fat (about 11 g, half the daily limit, all from full-fat paneer) and sodium (about 820 mg). Restaurant versions commonly add cashew paste, cream, butter and more oil and salt, often fry the paneer, and come with butter naan, so they are usually richer and saltier.

researchRating.basis: matar paneer is one of the most widely cooked paneer dishes in North Indian homes and appears on almost every Indian restaurant menu; it has its own Wikipedia article, many large recipe sites publish it (Veg Recipes of India has both a Punjabi and a dhaba-style version, Indian Healthy Recipes, Cook with Manali, whose recipe has at least 5 pages of reader comments, Ranveer Brar, Madhura's Recipe, Spice Up The Curry, Whisk Affair, Tea for Turmeric), and ready-to-eat packs are sold by Haldiram's and Kitchens of India. Swiggy listings found carry 4.2–4.8 dish ratings, which are not used. Points off because it is seen as an "everyday" rather than a special dish, and rubbery paneer and sour, under-cooked gravy are common home-cook complaints. Search-result snippets were the only access to these sites this run, so vote counts could not be read.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 2 days (cool within 1 hour). Freezer: up to 1 month (est.), though thawed paneer turns slightly spongy. Reheat in a pan on low with 2–3 tbsp water, stirring gently, until it just bubbles (the gravy thickens and the peas absorb liquid in the fridge); or microwave in 1-minute bursts, stirring between. Do not boil hard, or the paneer hardens.
leftoverRemix: Matar paneer stuffed paratha or toastie. Boil down the leftover curry in a pan until almost dry, mash it roughly with a fork, add chopped onion, coriander and a pinch of chaat masala, and use it as a stuffing for a paratha or between two slices of bread in a sandwich toaster with a little butter. The peas and paneer give a filling, high-protein breakfast.
burnOff: about 5.7 km of running (400 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 8 km of brisk walking (about 1 hour 35 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With 2 phulkas (about 580 kcal): about 8.3 km running or 11.6 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: green peas (a legume), onion, garlic, turmeric and garam masala are avoided in the common vrat rule set; paneer alone is allowed, but without peas it is a different dish (paneer bhurji/vrat paneer).

ekadashi.reason: green peas are a pulse/legume, avoided on Ekadashi in the most common rule set, along with onion and garlic.

jain.reason: skip onion, garlic and fresh ginger (root vegetables); use sonth and a tomato-only gravy.

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; moderately salty and protein-rich, it suits iftar dinner with roti; for sehri, eat it with roti and plenty of water because of the sodium.

jain.reason: skip onion and garlic, and use dry ginger powder (sonth) instead of fresh ginger; paneer and green peas are allowed (see Jain variant).

vegan.reason: paneer 75 g → pressed firm tofu 90 g; no other dairy in the main recipe (see Vegan variant).

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, so it fits a pescatarian diet.

sattvik.reason: skip onion and garlic and cook the gravy on tomato with fresh ginger (or use the Jain variant's gravy).

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, maida, rava or besan, and the main recipe uses no hing; if you add hing, use a gluten-free one, as most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour.

dairyFree.reason: paneer is the only dairy; use pressed firm tofu (Vegan variant).

description: A vegetarian, gluten-free Punjabi home curry of paneer and green peas in onion-tomato gravy; Jain, vegan and low-fat versions below.

variants.name: Jain Matar Paneer (no onion, garlic or fresh ginger)
Light Matar Paneer (low-fat paneer, 1 tsp oil)
